newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end sharply up, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end sharply up, seen rising.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed sharply higher on Tuesday after the central bank, responding to the stock market's recent rise and huge turnover, pledged again to adjust monetary policy at an "appropriate time".
Dealers expected a further firming on Wednesday.

The overnight interbank rate jumped to as high as 7.00 percent but eased a bit to settle at 6.977 percent against Monday's 6.657 close -- outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone but far below the record double-digit closes of late June.
The 30-day commercial paper was at 6.75 percent against 6.5 percent on Monday.

"The central bank will adjust its monetary policy at an appropriate time," a central bank official quoted deputy central bank governor Hsu Chia-tung as saying late on Monday after the stock index closed another seven-year high at 9,593.54 points.
The stock index rocketed to a seven-year intraday high in early trade on Tuesday but tumbled on late profit-taking and settled for a loss of 0.39 percent lower at 9,555.98 points.

By the time the dust had settled, stock turnover had spiked to a record T$262 billion, renewing concern in the market that the big stock market rally, which has doubled the index since March 1996, would be seen as driven by overly loose liquidity.
The central bank's recent moves to smooth the currency's recent depreciation and Tuesday's T$15 billion auction of treasury bills also served to tighten liquidity, dealers added.

Analysts say the central bank's repeated issuance of NCDs and treasury bills in recent weeks has been aimed mainly at cooling the stock rally, though the central bank has called its actions a more general response to fine-tune money supply.

In the bond market, yields for the benchmark 86/4 government bond jumped in early trading to an intra-day high of 6.0550 amid selling as investors worried over the central bank's palpable tightening of monetary policy.
The rise was short lived, however, as bond yields slid to an intra-day low of 5.9700 in late morning after the stock market's big early rise dissipated in the final hour.
Dealers said stock market volatility would continue to dominate sentiment in the bond market.
